s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with headache, emesis, and dizziness, following a recent surgical procedure
salient_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with gas-fluid level and gas bubbles
Significant leftward midline shift with subfalcine and left transtentorial herniation
key_facts: 45-year-old Filipino woman
2-day history of right-sided headache and emesis
Recent right tympanomastoidectomy for cholesteatoma 2 months prior
Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15
Afebrile and normotensive
Normal strength in all four extremities
Cranial nerves intact
Right mastoid region with a small gaping mastoidectomy wound and greenish discharge
Leukocyte count: 7.1 × 10⁹/L
C-reactive protein level: 500 mg/L
Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum cultured from the wound
Fungal, Nocardia, and Actinomyces cultures were negative

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Ring-enhancing lesion with gas-fluid level and gas bubbles on CT, recent surgical procedure, and positive cultures for Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum

shortlist.label: Subdural Empyema
shortlist.why_kept: Recent surgical procedure, greenish discharge, and high C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Epidural Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Recent surgical procedure, greenish discharge, and high C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis of the Skull
shortlist.why_kept: Recent tympanomastoidectomy, greenish discharge, and high C-reactive protein level

shortlist.label: Proteus Mirabilis Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Positive culture for Proteus mirabilis and ring-enhancing lesion on CT

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with right-sided headache, emesis, and a recent history of tympanomastoidectomy, combined with imaging findings of a ring-enhancing lesion with a gas-fluid level and gas bubbles in the right temporal lobe, is most consistent with a brain abscess. The cultured organisms, Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus gallinarum, are also commonly found in brain abscesses.

rejected.label: Subdural Empyema
rejected.why: While subdural empyema could explain some symptoms, the imaging findings of a localized, ring-enhancing lesion are more suggestive of an abscess.

rejected.label: Epidural Abscess
rejected.why: Epidural abscess typically presents with more localized signs of infection and does not usually cause the significant mass effect seen in this patient's imaging studies.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis of the Skull
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis of the skull could explain the greenish discharge from the mastoidectomy site, but it does not account for the intracranial findings on imaging.

rejected.label: Proteus Mirabilis Brain Abscess
rejected.why: While Proteus mirabilis is one of the cultured organisms, the diagnosis of brain abscess is more encompassing and explains the clinical and imaging findings better than specifying the organism alone.
